result.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models
result.summary: We introduce a predictive world model for electronic health records (EHR) that represents patient histories as action conditioned latent trajectories. Rather than modeling clinical events solely through autoregressive token prediction, our framework explicitly separates patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution through a state and action conditioned transition operator. At its core is a state dependent linearization predictor that propagates local changes in latent patient state, enabling time resolved prediction, multi step rollout, and action conditioned simulation. Empirically, we show that generated latent trajectories preserve downstream predictive signal, temporal structure, and subgroup level statistical relationships present in encoder derived representations. We further decode free running rollouts into the original clinical feature space and evaluate future clinical measurements against observed values using task matched forecasting baselines, demonstrating that the learned dynamics retain predictive information beyond latent space agreement. Across binary classification and time to event tasks, EHR WM achieves competitive, though task dependent, performance relative to substantially larger EHR foundation models while using a 30x smaller parameter footprint. Finally, perturbing observed action sequences produces corresponding changes in generated trajectories, demonstrating the action sensitivity of the learned dynamics. Together, these results support world modeling as a complementary framework for learning explicit, time indexed representations of patient evolution from longitudinal EHR.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 EHR 世界模型，将患者病史表示为动作条件化的 latent 轨迹：把患者状态与临床动作显式分离，用状态—动作条件转移算子并配合状态相关的线性化预测器实现多步 rollout 与动作条件模拟，在分类和时间到事件任务上以约 30 倍更小参数量取得有竞争力的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属医疗时序建模、无视觉与推理链，但其「状态/动作分离 + latent 转移算子 + 多步 rollout + 动作扰动敏感性」的可供核查线索，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的更新机制与轨迹监督设计提供参照。
